groups.title: Overview
paragraphs: Project ReCharge is a student-led circular-economy initiative addressing lithium-ion cells discarded in disposable vape devices. It combines responsible collection and battery recovery with research into safe reuse, recycling pathways and a prototype powerbank called the Phoenix Pack.

groups.title: Mission
paragraphs: Reclaim lithium. Reduce waste. Recharge the future.

groups.title: Current position
paragraphs: The initiative has demonstrated collection activity and a working powerbank prototype. A capstone automation effort is exploring repeatable assembly of a revised powerbank design. Product commercialization, deployment and automated production remain development goals rather than established operating capabilities.

groups.title: Key objectives
paragraphs: Divert disposable vape devices from improper disposal; establish controlled handling and recycling routes; evaluate reclaimed cells for potential reuse; develop a manufacturable powerbank; test automated assembly; and build an economically and environmentally sustainable service model.

groups.title: Waste stream
paragraphs: Disposable vape products contain lithium-ion cells alongside plastics, electronics and other components. Improper disposal can waste recoverable materials and create fire and environmental risks. Exact national disposal volumes and global recycling percentages cited in earlier project materials require source verification before external publication.

groups.title: Local validation
paragraphs: An earlier student survey reported approximately 60% of respondents had used a vape and approximately 6% disposed of devices properly. Survey sample size, wording, collection period and denominator should be preserved with the raw results before using these figures in formal claims.

groups.title: Collection evidence
paragraphs: A campus collection effort recovered more than 76 devices over three days. Retain dated collection logs, photographs, counts by category and final downstream disposition records to support this outcome.

groups.title: In scope
paragraphs: Awareness campaigns; controlled collection; sorting and inspection; battery characterization by trained personnel; feasibility evaluation; powerbank mechanical/electrical prototyping; robotic assembly concept; pilot business model; impact measurement.

groups.title: Out of scope until validated
paragraphs: Unsupervised opening of damaged vape devices; consumer distribution of unqualified reused cells; claims of certification; automated cell recovery from vape housings without an independently reviewed hazard analysis; and broad commercial rollout.

groups.title: Success criteria
paragraphs: Demonstrated safe collection and documented recycler handoff; reproducible engineering tests; an approved product design; reliable automated placement/assembly trials; traceable pilot metrics; and verified unit economics.

groups.title: Collection
paragraphs: Receive intact devices in appropriately selected fire-resistant collection containers under a documented collection protocol. Label collection points and prevent contamination with unrelated waste.

groups.title: Intake and segregation
paragraphs: Record quantities, device condition and collection location. Quarantine visibly compromised items and use an approved recycler or qualified specialist for disposition.

groups.title: Recovery decision
paragraphs: Only qualified personnel following an approved battery-safety procedure should determine whether cells can be safely recovered and assessed. Reuse eligibility must not be assumed from visual condition alone.

groups.title: Disposition
paragraphs: Route rejected cells and other device fractions to appropriate licensed or otherwise verified recycling partners. Maintain custody and weight/count records.

groups.title: Manufacturing route
paragraphs: Only individually qualified, traceable cells would proceed to a validated powerbank build process. The manufacturing process is separate from hazardous-device dismantling.

groups.title: Product description
paragraphs: Phoenix Pack is a rechargeable powerbank concept using recovered lithium-ion cells where safety and qualification permit. Its purpose is to turn a difficult waste stream into a visible, useful demonstration of circular material recovery.

groups.title: Defined assembly parts
paragraphs: The revised prototype is divided into four main parts: bottom casing, top casing, circuit board and batteries. Cells are arranged in alignment to simplify robotic placement and electrical interconnection.

groups.title: Battery connections
paragraphs: The design direction uses friction- or pressure-fit electrical contacts rather than soldering directly to the cells, reducing assembly heat exposure. Contact resistance, retention force, vibration tolerance, oxidation, short-circuit protection and long-term reliability require validation.

groups.title: Unconfirmed specifications
paragraphs: Cell chemistry, dimensions, capacity, quantity, series/parallel arrangement, protection IC, charge/discharge limits, connector types, USB output ratings, thermal design and enclosure material are all To verify. No performance rating should be published until measured.

groups.title: Electrical functions
paragraphs: The board design must address cell protection, overcharge/overdischarge, overcurrent, short circuit, temperature monitoring as appropriate, charging control and regulated output. Requirements depend on actual cell configuration and chemistry.

groups.title: Reuse qualification
paragraphs: A documented battery acceptance program should consider identity/chemistry, physical damage, voltage, capacity, internal resistance, self-discharge, history and compatibility. Thresholds must be defined by qualified engineering review and relevant standards—not inferred from this document.

groups.title: Design safeguards
paragraphs: Use insulating barriers, polarity-keyed placement, mechanically secure contacts, protected terminals, appropriate fusing/protection, strain relief, and enclosure features preventing access to energized conductors.

groups.title: Regulatory gate
paragraphs: Before any public lending, rental or sale, obtain specialist review of applicable Canadian electrical/product safety, lithium battery transport, recycling and consumer-product requirements, and appropriate independent testing/certification where required.

groups.title: Enclosure
paragraphs: The bottom casing locates and supports batteries and circuit board. The top casing closes and protects the assembly. CAD should include datums, fastening or snap-fit geometry, clearances, ventilation/thermal provisions and serviceability.

groups.title: Assembly-friendly design
paragraphs: Use consistent cell orientation, lead-ins, chamfers, locating bosses and accessible grasping surfaces. Avoid geometries requiring a robot to flex cells or force electrical contacts beyond validated insertion loads.

groups.title: Design outputs
paragraphs: Maintain controlled CAD files, exploded assembly, dimensioned drawings, material selection, tolerance stack-up, assembly instructions and engineering change records.

groups.title: Objective
paragraphs: Explore repeatable assembly of the four-part powerbank with robotic material handling, controlled placement and verification. The focus is design for automation, not the identity of individual team members.

groups.title: Proposed cell workflow
paragraphs: Present bottom casing in a repeatable fixture; locate casing; place prequalified cells in the aligned orientation; install the circuit board and engage validated pressure-fit contacts; fit top casing; inspect and transfer to an electrical test station.

groups.title: Equipment categories
paragraphs: Industrial robot or collaborative robot, end-effector/gripper, part feeders or trays, fixture/nest, PLC, discrete sensors, optional machine vision, guarding/interlocks, electrical test equipment and HMI. Exact models and installed devices remain To verify.

groups.title: Controls
paragraphs: PLC logic should coordinate station readiness, safe start, part-present signals, robot handshakes, fault states, recovery and test disposition. Robot programs should use validated frames, speed limits and collision checks.

groups.title: Major assembly challenges
paragraphs: Variation in reclaimed-cell size/condition; reliable orientation and grasping; consistent contact insertion force; electrical polarity verification; dimensional tolerance variation; enclosure closure; prevention of shorts; and dependable rejection/traceability.

groups.title: Safety boundary
paragraphs: Robot cell assembly should not be treated as permission to automate disassembly of hazardous disposable vape devices. Develop separate risk assessments and safeguards for each operation.

groups.title: Inspection stages
paragraphs: Incoming cell qualification; casing/PCB incoming inspection; part-presence and polarity checks; contact-engagement checks; enclosure inspection; electrical safety and functional tests; final traceability record.

groups.title: Test plan
paragraphs: Define test ID, purpose, fixture, instruments/calibration, sample size, acceptance limits, results, reviewer and corrective action. Candidate tests include contact resistance, output voltage, charging function, thermal behavior, drop/vibration, short-circuit protection and cycle endurance.

groups.title: Release control
paragraphs: No unit should enter student/public use without documented acceptance criteria, approved test results, safe-use instructions and product liability/regulatory review.

groups.title: Impact pathway
paragraphs: The initiative links responsible collection, material recovery, education and a tangible powerbank demonstration. Recycling remains the appropriate pathway for cells that cannot be responsibly reused.

groups.title: Measures
paragraphs: Track devices collected, cell mass and count, proportion rejected, recycler handoff, cells qualified for reuse, powerbanks built/tested, collection engagement and educational reach. Avoid equating collection volume with verified emissions savings.

groups.title: SDGs
paragraphs: Prior project materials identify contributions to multiple UN Sustainable Development Goals. Map each claimed SDG to a measurable project activity and supporting evidence before external reporting.

groups.title: Customers and beneficiaries
paragraphs: Students, educational institutions, campuses and other high-traffic facilities are potential beneficiaries. Proposed institutional payers and operating partners must be validated through interviews and pilots.

groups.title: Concept
paragraphs: A powerbank lending/rental kiosk could support short-term charging needs. Potential revenue includes rental fees and advertising; kiosk displays may also support public-service or emergency messaging subject to governance and technical validation.

groups.title: Economics
paragraphs: Build a cost model covering collection, qualified labor, cell testing/rejection, electronics, enclosure, automation, energy, quality assurance, certification, kiosk capital, maintenance, insurance, replacement and recycler fees. No break-even estimate is currently verified.

groups.title: Pilot
paragraphs: Start with a supervised, limited-access pilot only after product safety review, operational permissions, user instructions, maintenance processes and incident response are in place.

groups.title: Project history
paragraphs: ReCharge evolved from lithium recovery and awareness into the Phoenix Pack prototype and an automated manufacturing capstone. A collection drive and project showcases provided early traction.

groups.title: Reported recognition
paragraphs: Prior project records mention an Innovation & Impact Champion recognition, second place in the Canadian Tire Environmental Sustainability Challenge, Ford Innovation Showcase involvement, Red Bull Basement 2026 Canada idea recognition, and a St. Clair College innovation prize. Verify official event names, dates and award wording before publication.

groups.title: Partner needs
paragraphs: Potential partners include campus administration, student council, verified electronics/battery recyclers, engineering reviewers, insurers, kiosk host sites and manufacturing sponsors.

groups.title: Operating structure
paragraphs: Maintain accountable ownership of project management, mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, automation, procurement/budget, safety/quality, outreach and business development. Roles may be shared but decision authority should be explicit.

groups.title: Document management
paragraphs: Store source files in a shared controlled repository with version naming, revision log, reviewers and change approval. Keep public presentation material distinct from confidential test and supplier records.

groups.title: Continuity
paragraphs: Prepare onboarding notes, system diagrams, bill of materials, CAD and code repositories, vendor contacts, open risks, test evidence and next-step priorities so future students can continue development.

groups.title: Gate A — baseline
paragraphs: Confirm product requirements, device/cell constraints, safety review and controlled design files.

groups.title: Gate B — prototype
paragraphs: Complete mechanical/electrical integration and documented bench validation.

groups.title: Gate C — automation
paragraphs: Demonstrate repeatable assembly of representative safe components with recorded cycle time, yield and fault recovery.

groups.title: Gate D — product qualification
paragraphs: Complete required safety, reliability and compliance assessment.

groups.title: Gate E — supervised pilot
paragraphs: Secure approvals, implement operating procedures, collect utilization and incident data.

groups.title: Gate F — expansion
paragraphs: Validate economics, supply and recycler capacity, maintenance and governance before scaling.

groups.title: BOM fields
paragraphs: Part ID; description; revision; supplier; approved alternative; unit price; quantity; extended price; lead time; lifecycle status; and safety/quality notes.

groups.title: Cost tracking
paragraphs: Distinguish research costs, prototype costs, pilot costs and recurring production costs. Track cell rejection losses and testing labor, not merely purchased component prices.

groups.title: Funding
paragraphs: Document grants, prizes, sponsorships, in-kind equipment and restrictions. Maintain receipts and a dated budget-versus-actual register.

groups.title: Battery fire or thermal runaway — Critical
paragraphs: Control through qualified handling, quarantine, cell screening, engineering safeguards, appropriate storage and emergency planning. Owner and residual risk: To assign.

groups.title: Cell variability — High
paragraphs: Control through identification, acceptance testing, compatible-cell matching and traceability.

groups.title: Pressure-contact failure — High
paragraphs: Control through force/resistance validation, environmental tests and end-of-line checks.

groups.title: Robot collision or pinch hazard — High
paragraphs: Control through task-based risk assessment, guarding, interlocks, safe speeds and authorized access.

groups.title: Noncompliance / liability — Critical
paragraphs: Control through early regulatory review, third-party advice, documentation and release gates.

groups.title: Supply / business model uncertainty — Medium
paragraphs: Control through conservative forecasts, recycler agreements, pilot feedback and scenario analysis.

groups.title: Engineering
paragraphs: Confirm cell chemistry and geometry; establish qualified cell criteria; freeze electrical architecture; select contact system; determine enclosure material; validate BOM and CAD revisions.

groups.title: Automation
paragraphs: Inventory actual robot, PLC, sensors and fixtures; produce I/O list; define cell layout and gripping; draft sequence and fault handling; measure cycle time and yield.

groups.title: Operations
paragraphs: Approve collection and disposal SOPs; confirm recycler agreements; develop incident response; establish traceability and records retention.

groups.title: Commercial
paragraphs: Identify payer, kiosk host, rental rules, insurance and service model; estimate lifecycle cost and pilot budget.

groups.title: Evidence
paragraphs: Collect survey methodology, competition confirmations, prototype photos, engineering reports, test results and source references.

groups.title: Incoming battery record
paragraphs: Record ID | source batch | receipt date | cell identifier | chemistry | physical condition | screening outcome | disposition | inspector.

groups.title: Assembly test record
paragraphs: Build ID | CAD/PCB revisions | cell IDs | station/operator | date | electrical test results | visual result | deviations | release status.

groups.title: Engineering change request
paragraphs: Change ID | problem | affected documents | risk impact | proposed revision | reviewer | approval | effective date.

groups.title: Incident / near-miss record
paragraphs: Date | location | equipment | event | immediate controls | personnel notified | investigation | corrective action | closure.

groups.title: Evidence and reference log
paragraphs: Claim | source document/link | author | date | verification status | approved external wording.

groups.title: BOM
paragraphs: Bill of Materials — controlled list of components, quantities and purchasing details.

groups.title: PLC
paragraphs: Programmable Logic Controller — industrial controller coordinating station logic and signals.

groups.title: HMI
paragraphs: Human–Machine Interface — controls and status display for operators.

groups.title: Traceability
paragraphs: Ability to connect each finished assembly to component lots, inspections and tests.

groups.title: Pressure-fit contact
paragraphs: Mechanical electrical connection established by controlled contact force rather than direct cell soldering.
